tickets.title: Logo mark
tickets.why: You want one simple mark to sign any photo (a venue shot, a story) without a full artwork layer.
tickets.serves: Photo posts, stories, thumbnail corner, the sting, gig announcements, Canva Brand Kit logo. Marketing: gig and press material.
tickets.question: Direction: the inch mark (ruler tick), lowercase wordmark, monogram, or another. Size and placement rules. When the mark is used versus the no-text-in-artwork rule (two rules, two objects).
tickets.decision: Working set, not final art (Amir will try drawing it by hand, maybe in Canva). Direction: the RING. WORDMARK: 'Inch of Shadow' in Marcellus mixed case with an obelisk as the I, casting its shadow at the foot. MARK: a thorn ring (crown of thorns as halo and as cycle), used alone wherever the name does not fit: profile picture, stamp, corner of a photo. CAPITALS VERSION: 'INCH OF SHADOW' spaced, with the thorn ring as the O, for seals and back prints. Do not combine the obelisk I and the ring O in one lockup, it crowds. Three-word name is handled by the stacked block INCH / OF / SHADOW when a compact shape is needed. RULE: never abbreviate as IOS or IoS (Apple). Rejected: literal inch symbol, ruler tick, half shadow circle, moon phases, snake ouroboros, classic laurel (Fred Perry), monogram with letters. Drafts kept in docs/brand/mark/mark-drafts-v4.html and .png; the vectors are code-drawn and still look mechanical, final art to be hand drawn.
notes: 2026-09-13 opened. Ask for references first.

Recommendation: the found-image route fits him best (cycles, light against dark), the inch mark is the literal route, the Marcellus wordmark is needed either way.

2026-09-19 round 2 rendered (thorn, dividers, gnomon, tuning fork, obelisk with shadow, dial plate; each as seal with the lyric as sundial motto, name lockup with the object as the I, 34px test, signed on a photo). Three routes offered: rebuild the vectors properly, start from real public domain engravings (needs his go to download), or generate reference art with the paid image tool. Awaiting his choice.

Model is Lana Del Rey's design language, not her sound: familiar cultural symbols (America, flag, colours), luxury broadcast, luxury type (Honeymoon), styling swinging between distant luxury and city rock girl. Test: would a stranger feel something in one second without an explanation.

2026-09-19 consequence for the mark: gnomon and obelisk are smart but cold and niche. Next round should test mass-legible theological and mythological symbols drawn in engraving style, keeping the shadow idea.

2026-09-21 REOPENED by Amir: he wants to focus on the logo and asked to be GUIDED (he is not a designer; the inspiration sites were too hard to use alone), with questions and the 'world' pointed out to him. 2026-09-21 round 2 answers: the symbol may come from the name's own idea, a sacred or myth sign, or letters as a shape (not a pure shape); he wants rough sketches from Claude to react to; colour: one colour always, plus an optional special version (foil, gradient) for special items. 2026-09-21 Amir on round C: 'basically none'. The cross/sword is a cool idea, maybe in the future, not as the first logo. RULE from him: AVOID familiar symbols from familiar religions; they do not engage and do not attach to the brand. 2026-09-21 ROUND D shown (other kinds of mark, nothing borrowed): 20 the name drawn only by its shadow, 21 the name sinking into shadow (solid above, thin fading lines below), 22 the sound (two seconds of The Deceiver from 1:02 drawn round a circle; a first version stacked lines like Unknown Pleasures and was changed before showing because it copied Joy Division), 23 his sunglasses, 24 an inch of shadow taken literally (a light field with one dark band at its foot; also reads as a Polaroid), 25 the name in Impact, outlined, with a long cast shadow. 2026-09-21 Amir: 'go wider'. ROUND E shown, rough and hand-made kinds: 26 an ink blot folded in half (seeded, unique), 27 a rubber stamp with uneven ink, 28 the name sprayed through a stencil (horizontal stencil bridges were tried first and dropped, they read as crossed out), 29 the name photocopied until it breaks up, 30 typed on a typewriter, lower case with a full stop, 31 the name at one bit, blocky pixels. 2026-09-21 Amir: 'give me last round'. ROUND F, the last, shown: the NAME itself as the logo, six ways: 32 neon (hollow tubes), 33 cut-out (the name knocked out of a black block), 34 the column (letter under letter, a record spine), 35 the reflection (the name and its fading reflection, like the statue on The Deceiver), 36 light and shadow (INCH OF solid, SHADOW outlined), 37 the diagonal (heavy condensed italic rising, from his reference 38). 37 directions in six rounds, all in references/look02/. 2026-09-22 Amir's picks across rounds: round C keep 14 (the sword/cross, earlier said 'maybe in the future, not the first one'); round D keep 20 (the name in its shadow), 21 (the name sinking), 25 (the long shadow in Impact); round E keep 27 to 31 (stamp, spray, photocopy, typewriter, bitmap). 2026-09-22 ROUND G shown (another last one, new processes for the name): 38 halftone (dots growing into shadow lower down), 39 embossed label tape, 40 glitch (bands slipping sideways), 41 weathered stone inscription, 42 dot-matrix print, 43 a torn paper strip with the name cut out. 43 directions in seven rounds, references/look02/.

2026-09-23 Amir added 43 (the torn strip) to the shortlist and asked what Claude thinks of all his picks. Claude's read, given to him: the 11 picks are two different kinds of thing. SYMBOLS that can live alone and small (the eclipse, the inch mark, and the sword, which he already parked for later) and TREATMENTS of the name (20, 21, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 43), which are one object, the wordmark, wearing different surfaces. Only one treatment can be chosen. Two honest critiques: (1) he answered 'clean and exact' in the interview but picks rough print almost every time, so the rough world is the real answer; (2) most of the treatments belong to a scene (zine, DIY, post-punk) rather than to him, while 20 and 21 MEAN the name and are his alone. Also practical: photocopy, spray and halftone die at small sizes and in embroidery; stamp, bitmap, long shadow and torn strip hold. Proposal put to him: keep the system as wordmark plus a small mark, and narrow to three pairs to test at small size.

2026-09-23 SCOPE from Amir: for now only two places matter, a T-shirt and artwork. No pins, caps or other merch, no thinking far ahead. What he is looking for is 'a general language': a regular way to represent Inch of Shadow, the name and the mark together. All twelve picks drawn side by side at the same size, then each one on a T-shirt and on a cover (references/look02/picks_side_by_side.jpg, picks_in_place_1.jpg, picks_in_place_2.jpg). 2026-09-23 the twelve picks sorted into FOUR FAMILIES and drawn big, one sheet each (references/look02/picks_family_1..4.jpg, built by families.py): (1) THE MARKS, a sign with no letters, travels next to the name: eclipse, inch mark, sword. (2) THE NAME AS SHADOW, the name carries the idea and nobody else can use it: 20, 21, 25. (3) PRESSED AND PRINTED, ink on paper, warm and human: stamp, photocopy, typewriter, torn strip. (4) STREET AND SCREEN, hard edges, sprayed or pixels: spray, bitmap. The choice is one family for the name plus, if he wants, one mark from family 1.

Sheets: references/look02/v2/ (v2_all.jpg, v2_family_1..4.jpg with before and now), script logo_v2.py.

2026-09-24 Amir on v2. MARKS: loves them; the SWORD is removed from the logo, kept for a T-shirt or other merch later. The eclipse and the inch mark stay and should be adapted and made more beautiful. NAMES: loves 20 (the name in its shadow) and 21 (the name sinking); 25 (long shadow) he likes but finds generic, still thinking. FACE: 'the best font is 43, or 28, or even 29', he likes the font of family 3. Note: 43 and 28 are the same typeface, Impact (the one he liked from his Cure reference 38); 29 is Marcellus made gritty by the photocopy. Next round: refined variants of the two marks, and 20 and 21 set in Impact clean, Impact with print grit, and Marcellus with print grit.

2026-09-24 V3 shown (references/look02/v3/). MARKS refined, four each: eclipse A as v2, B the shadow rises (disc high, light a thin smile at the bottom), C no ring, a full disc and a hairline crescent like a moon's edge, D the disc pushes through the ring and breaks the circle; inch mark A as v2, B upright wedges like a typographer's prime, C slanted wedges (the real double prime), D the shadow stroke in fine lines. NAMES 20 and 21 each in Impact, Impact with print grit, and Marcellus with print grit (29's look); on 21 the grit is gentler so the thinning lines survive.

2026-09-24 Amir: focus on the MOON. It replaces the o of 'of', or maybe the o of 'Shadow'. Asked for it 'more engraving'. Drawn locally (references/look02/moon/, moon.py): E1 an engraved sphere, curved lines of latitude that thicken into the shadow, lit side bare paper; E2 the engraved eclipse, a fine ring and the shadow disc in concentric lines (it also reads as a record); E3 a crescent of paper, the rest cross-hatched. Set as the o in 'of' and in 'Shadow', in Marcellus and in Impact, with E1 and E2, each also shown small. Honest limit recorded: at small size the engraving closes up into a grey dot, so an engraved logo always needs a flat twin for small uses.

2026-09-25 Amir on the moon round: the moon as the O is 'the obvious', and all the drafts are 'very, very obvious' and need improving; as a FIRST DRAFT it is fine to keep them that way. Family for the name: still undecided. The INCH MARK is removed for now, kept in memory. The moon-O set in the fonts read to him like 'a high-tech brain'. area_rule: Show tickets to Amir as '<emoji> <Area> <area_no>' (e.g. '🎵 Release 2'). Old ids stay for code, commits and history only. Legend: plans/AREAS.md Priority (Amir 2026-11-05): each open ticket has bucket (now/next/parked/routine), who (amir 🙋 / claude 🎃 / auto 🤖), label, next_step and chrome (true = work happens in Amir's Chrome). Max 3 'now' per area; it is a cap, not a quota: an area with nothing urgent (e.g. Studio) has 0 'now'. Each area's parent chat sets its own buckets; the System chat merges them. One loop (2026-11-05): every ticket names the metric it moves (plans/targets.json key or 'none' with metric_note) and carries updated; RM /tickets?group=metric shows the board by number. One axis (System 78, 2026-11-06): bucket is the priority; the old priority P1-P3 is no longer stored and is derived from the bucket on RM /tickets only (now = P1, next = P2, parked and routine = P3). Every ticket also carries done_means (one line: what is true when it closes; done_means_by says who wrote it, 'claude' = derived from title/helps/next_step, not Amir's wording).

fields.metric: key from plans/targets.json metrics that this ticket moves, or 'none'
fields.metric_note: when metric is 'none': five words on why no number moves
fields.updated: ISO date of the last edit to this ticket (staleness check)
fields.bucket: now | next | parked | routine: the one priority axis (Amir 2026-11-05; P1-P3 dropped 2026-11-06)
fields.who: amir | claude | auto: who moves it next
fields.next_step: the next step or the blocker, one line
fields.label: short platform + topic name shown with the number, e.g. 'Bandcamp Friday'
fields.chrome: true when the work happens in Amir's Chrome (one shared browser, one job at a time, outside automation windows)
fields.done_means: one line: what is true when the ticket closes
fields.done_means_by: amir | claude: who wrote done_means ('claude' = derived from title/helps/next_step, not Amir's wording)
